hints: The base of the logarithm becomes the base of the exponent.
The logarithm equals the exponent.

questions.feedbackIfWrong: The common logarithm $\log x$ has base 10.
questions.prompt: The logarithm $\log x$ without a written base is understood to have base ___.
hints: It is called the common logarithm.
Our number system is base 10.
Ask: 2 raised to what power equals 16?
Count the factors: $2 \cdot 2 \cdot 2 \cdot 2 = 16$.
Base of the power is the base of the log.
The exponent is what the log equals.
questions.prompt: Rewrite $3^4 = 81$ in logarithmic form. (Use format log_3 81 = 4)

hints: The argument of a logarithm must be positive.
Any number to the zero power equals 1.
questions.prompt: The value of $\log_b 1$ for any positive base $b$ (with $b \neq 1$) is always ___.

hints: This uses the inverse property $b^{\log_b x} = x$.
Base 10 and log base 10 cancel.

questions.prompt: Simplify $\log_5 25^{x}$. (Enter the expression in terms of x, e.g., 2x)
hints: Write 25 as $5^2$.
Then use $\log_5 (5^2)^x = \log_5 5^{2x}$.
The inverse of an exponential function is a logarithmic function.
The base stays the same.

questions.prompt: The graph of $y = \log_b x$ has a vertical asymptote at $x =$ ___.
hints: It is the $y$-axis.
The log function is undefined for $x \le 0$.
Rewrite in exponential form: $3^4 = x$.
3 to the 4th power.

questions.prompt: Which point lies on the graph of $y = \log_5 x$?
hints: The $x$-intercept of a log function is at $x=1$.
Because $\log_b 1 = 0$.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: Since $\log_5 1 = 0$, the point $(1,0)$ is on the graph.

questions.prompt: Use a calculator to find $\ln 0.5$ to two decimal places. (Enter a number, e.g., -0.69)
hints: Press LN, then 0.5, ENTER.
The natural log of a number less than 1 is negative.

questions.feedbackIfWrong: The range of a logarithmic function is all real numbers.
questions.prompt: What is the range of $f(x) = \log_2 x$?
hints: Log functions can output any real number.
They are the inverse of exponentials which have range $y>0$.
The natural log is only defined for positive inputs.
questions.prompt: For $f(x) = \ln(x-2)$, the argument $x-2$ must be greater than ___.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: The argument must be positive, so $x-2 > 0$.
